allowed_role: A-table independent establishment and HR-labor management evidence layer
C-table independent worker-side function, support-need, participation, and satisfaction evidence layer
restricted narrative evidence layer after redaction and narrative-unit staging

strengths.description: A/B/C tables allow establishment, supervisor, and disabled-worker perspectives to be compared for many pairs.
A alone has establishment and HR-labor-management coverage, including accommodation burden perception, employment reasons, employment challenges, and external expert advice/consultation use.

B and C include dense structured items on worksite contact points, supports, task performance, communication, mobility, commuting, health/self-care, interpersonal relations, emergency preparedness, and daily living.

B alone has unusually detailed supervisor/workplace-side structured coverage of support states, task-contact problems, occupational-life constraints, assistive devices, job context, and external support context; it should be preserved as a workplace-perspective layer, not only as a B/C contrast source.
B support implementation/needed/not-needed states can be contrasted with C need/usefulness states after category and item alignment QA.
C alone has worker-side detailed function-condition windows, support need/usefulness ratings, job-content context, response-method flags, assistive-device use, and job satisfaction.

A/B/C include substantial narrative fields: A establishment added context and employment-management notes, B work-content/support-practice/external-support narratives, and C work-content/support-method/open-need narratives. These should enter SCIMA/FCHMA only through redaction and narrative-unit staging.
B constraints/problems plus C job satisfaction and support usefulness can test participation quality without treating job continuation as sufficient.
Physical, sensory, internal, and intellectual disability windows appear rich enough for diversity-conditioned structural comparison.

blind_spots.description: The data reflects 2001 labor-market, policy, support-service, and workplace-design contexts.
No rare-disease source family is present; health-time claims must not be generalized to current rare-disease employment support.
Mental disability appears only in a pre-employment-obligation historical context and should be treated as a limited condition window.
The request scheme asked establishments to select up to three disabled workers, generally prioritizing heavier disability degree and diversity when needed.
The local README cautions that disabled-worker-number linkage is not necessarily certain; B/C disability and severity mismatch must be QA flags.
Supervisor and worker responses are different actor perspectives, not interchangeable measurements of one truth.
C includes diagnosis/health-condition text and A/B/C include free text; row-level text must not be quoted or exported.

hard_repair_before_analysis: coded values outside dictionary labels unless recoded by documented missing/other-code policy
unreviewed item-number matching between B and C support items
soft_flag_not_default_exclusion: C non-self or assisted answer method
preserve_as_signal: supervisor-worker support need differences after alignment QA
participation-quality differences between constraints, support usefulness, and satisfaction

required_before_scima_fchma_interpretati: redaction and content-hash staging for narrative units before LLM reading
required_before_knowledge_network_merge: human review or explicit unreviewed contrast status
